html:
A king of Kush who ruled from Napata, in today's Sudan, and conquered Egypt, founding its 25th Dynasty. His birth date is unknown; the chart shows his reign, about 744 to 714 BCE.

Piye was the son of King Kashta, who had already pushed Kushite power north toward Thebes. Egypt at the time was split among rival kings and chiefs. When a prince of the Nile Delta named Tefnakhte began conquering his neighbours, Piye sent his army north and then came himself. The campaign is told under Piye of Kush conquers Egypt.

He told the story on a great granite stela set up in the temple of Amun at Jebel Barkal. It shows him as a pious king who honoured Egypt's gods and took a special interest in horses.

After his victory Piye went home to Napata. He was buried under a pyramid at el-Kurru, the first king of Kush to revive that Egyptian custom, with his favourite horses buried nearby. His successors, among them Taharqa, ruled Egypt until the Assyrians drove them out. They were the 25th Dynasty.
